I found one bug in the uncommitted change to `bash_completionsV2.go`. I didn't run it.

**`bash_completionsV2.go:194` — empty completion lines are no longer skipped.**
- **Old code:** `comp=$(compgen -W "$comp" -- "$cur"); [[ -z $comp ]] && continue`. An empty or whitespace-only line gave an empty `comp`, so the loop skipped it.
- **New code:** `[[ $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue`. With an empty `$cur`, which is the usual case right after a space, `""` matches the prefix `""`. So any blank line, or any line that is only a tab and a description, now goes into `COMPREPLY` as an empty candidate.
- **Failure case:** the program's completion output contains a blank line, and at least one other line has a description. This happens when the output is `foo\tdesc\n\nbar\tdesc`, or when the output ends with a trailing newline. The user presses Tab on `prog <TAB>`. The old code listed only `foo` and `bar`. The new code also adds an empty entry. That shows up as a blank row in the list. It can also turn a single match into two, so the single-match path that strips the description and inserts the word no longer runs.
- **Fix:** also skip empty values, for example `[[ -n $comp && $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue`.

**Smaller inconsistency:** the no-description fast path at line 183 still filters with `compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur"`. The description path now uses a literal prefix match instead. They can disagree on entries with special characters. `compgen -W` word-splits and expands its argument, so a candidate with a space or a `$` is handled differently by the two paths. The new path's literal match is arguably the more correct of the two. Still, the same completion list can now give different results depending on whether any entry has a description.
